name: Question 13
worked_solution:
Let's first factor the denominator of the integrand:

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-12x+4}{{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+4x}=\frac{4{x}^{2}-12x+4}{x(x-2)^{2}}
$$

We must convert the integrand into a sum of partial fractions:

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-12x+4}{x(x-2)^{2}}=\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{x-2}+\frac{C}{(x-2)^{2}}
$$

To determine the coefficients $A,B$ and $C,$ we first multiply both sides of the above equation by $x(x-2)^{2}$ and get

$$
4{x}^{2}-12x+4=A(x-2)^{2}+Bx(x-2)+Cx.
$$

Plugging in $x=2,$ we can eliminate $A$ and $B$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(2)^{2}-12(2)+4 & =A(2-2)^{2}+B(2)(2-2)+C(2) \\ -4 & =2C \\ C & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, plugging in $x=0,$ we can eliminate $B$ and $C$ and solve for $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(0)^{2}-12(0)+4 & =A(0-2)^{2}+B(0)(0-2)+C(0) \\ 4 & =4A \\ A & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, plugging in $x=1$ and substituting the known values of $A$ and $C,$ we can solve for $B:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4(1)^{2}-12(1)+4 & =A(1-2)^{2}+B(1)(1-2)+C(1) \\ -4 & =A-B+C \\ -4 & =1-B+(-2) \\ -3 & =-B \\ B & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integrand as the partial sum

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-12x+4}{{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+4x}=\frac{1}{x}+\frac{3}{x-2}-\frac{2}{(x-2)^{2}}.
$$

Finally, we integrate this expression term by term to get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-12x+4}{{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+4x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{x}+\frac{3}{x-2}-\frac{2}{(x-2)^{2}})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x+3\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x-2\int \frac{1}{(x-2)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡|x|+3\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|+\frac{2}{x-2}+K,\end{aligned}
$$

where $K$ is an integral constant.
